packets.title: Connect modular appearances to owned rebel equipment

packets.title: Map modular gear to tactical sprite appearance layers
packets.acceptance: Carrier/pack/headgear silhouettes resolve through existing paper-doll layers; 3D assets do not replace the established tactical renderer.

packets.title: Validate and release the expanded modular catalogue
packets.acceptance: All published families pass explicit coverage matrix, worst-case kit/weapon stacks, migrations, accessible editor and measured load/memory budgets; gameplay adapters do not block this gallery release.

packets.title: Campaign save v1: one versioned state for world, band, stash and log; migrate the tactical squad and Rebel Band saves; storage adapter
packets.acceptance: shared/campaign/state.js is pure and versioned; parp-squad-v1 and the Rebel Band save migrate into it; unit tests cover new, load, migrate and corrupt input.

packets.title: Mission bridge: deployment and result payloads, kit reserved on launch, result settled exactly once, refresh mid-mission counts as withdrawn
packets.acceptance: convoy/?campaign&encounter reads a deployment from the save and writes one result; settling twice is a no-op; a reload mid-mission settles as withdrawn; practice mode unchanged.

packets.title: The band on the map: navigation grid from the heightfield and roads, click to move, route preview, terrain speeds, follow camera
packets.acceptance: Clicking land moves the player party along a valid path (never through sea); roads faster, snow and forest slower; path tests on map/island.js.

packets.title: Campaign clock: pause and three speeds, day and night tint and sight, pause on encounters and menus
packets.acceptance: Space pauses, 1-3 set speed; night tint and reduced sight; opening a menu or encounter stops time; reduced motion respected.

packets.title: World simulation core: seeded headless parties with goals, speeds and sight; save and restore; determinism tests
packets.acceptance: shared/campaign/world.js steps without a renderer; same seed and orders give the same world; state round-trips through the save.

packets.title: Convoys on the map: spawn at Invader seats, road routes, cargo manifest and escort on the nameplate, resupply on arrival
packets.acceptance: Convoys follow ROADS between settlements; their manifest and escort are visible; an arrival raises the garrison; unit tests.

packets.title: Hunters and heat: patrols, hunter columns spawned by heat, map sight (night, forest, band size), last-seen tracking, losing them
packets.acceptance: Attacks raise heat and hunters; hunters chase the last-seen point and can lose you; sight radii shown on the map; harness metrics for hunts per day.

packets.title: Encounters: contact rules and the encounter panel (Attack, Prepare ambush, Withdraw with a rearguard, Leave)
packets.acceptance: Contact pauses time and opens a keyboard-operable panel with both sides' strength and the ground; each option leads to a mission or a map outcome.

packets.title: Convoy encounter launches the Convoy Ambush, set up from the convoy party (vehicles, escort, cargo, time, ambush start); result back to the map
packets.acceptance: A map convoy opens the convoy level with its escort and vehicles; win leaves a wreck and captures cargo; loss lets it pass; e2e map to mission to map.

packets.title: Settlement encounter launches the Compound Assault: defenders from garrison and militia, variants per settlement kind, night infiltration
packets.acceptance: Marching on an Invader settlement opens the compound level scaled to its garrison; success raids or captures it on the map.

packets.title: Caught by an army launches the Rebel Base Defence: cave level at camp, new hasty-defence variant in the open
packets.acceptance: A hunter touching the band at Oros Camp opens the cave defence with waves from its strength; in the open, a field defence level; overrun and victory both change the map. An overrun follows TAC-K-03: half of each camp stack lost (rounded down), fallen fighters wounded, fall back to the nearest friendly settlement, heat halved.

packets.title: Deploy screen: pick up to four fighters from the band; one squad model shared by the band and the missions
packets.acceptance: Before a mission the player picks fighters from the band; their classes, abilities and kit appear in the mission; the rest stay on the map.

packets.title: Return to the map: settle casualties, wounds, experience, kills and aftermath (wreck, smoke); autosave and result toast
packets.acceptance: The debrief returns to the map, which applies the result once and shows it in the world and a toast; reload-safe.

packets.title: Loot into the band: cargo manifest and level loot into the campaign stash, with its source
packets.acceptance: Debrief loot appears in the band stash labelled with where it came from; convoy loot follows the manifest.

packets.title: The band screen on the campaign save, opened from the map (P); promotions with experience and stolen kit
packets.acceptance: band/ reads and writes the campaign state; promoting consumes the stash kit; standalone Rebel Band demo still works.

packets.title: Owned guns in the Weapon Modder: only owned attachments selectable, locked ones say where they drop; assign a build to a fighter

packets.title: Looks from kit: a fighter's class and owned wearables set the Operator Customiser look and the map figure
packets.acceptance: Promoting a fighter or giving them a helmet changes their look in the customiser and on the map.

packets.title: Recruits and barter at friendly villages
packets.acceptance: Neutral and liberated villages barter item for item from a seeded weekly stock (TAC-K-01); liberated villages offer tier-1 recruits; no trader at camp in a campaign.

packets.title: Territory: capture settlements, what they give (recruits, food, rest), Invader counter-attacks to retake them
packets.acceptance: A captured settlement turns its province to the Resistance and gives its benefits; the Invader sends a party to retake it.

packets.title: Escalation director: Invader response tiers drive hunters, mission difficulty and enemy kit
packets.acceptance: Response tier rises with Resistance strength; tiers change hunter size, mission difficulty and enemy kit; harness shows the curve.

packets.title: Endgame and defeat: the Fort Orion assault, the camp-overrun defeat, campaign summary
packets.acceptance: Taking the last Invader seat opens the final assault; winning or losing the campaign ends in a summary screen; a new campaign can start.

packets.title: Auto-resolve for small, lopsided fights, with the odds shown first
packets.acceptance: Offered only at 2.5x strength or against a lone patrol, never for camp defence, captures or the finale; odds and expected wounds shown first; results slightly worse than played (TAC-K-02); used by the harness.

packets.title: Campaign harness: fifty seeded headless campaigns with auto-resolve, pacing report and a tuning pass
packets.acceptance: tools/campaign/bench.mjs reports time to first encounter, first promotion, hunts per day and stash growth against the roadmap targets.

packets.title: Campaign end-to-end tests and performance: map to mission to map, two tabs and refresh safety, map at 30 fps on a mid phone
packets.acceptance: Smoke covers a full campaign round trip; double settlement impossible across tabs; map frame budget measured.

packets.title: First-campaign prompts, design doc campaign section, changelog and index entry
packets.acceptance: A new player is guided through move, encounter, loot and promote; the design doc describes the campaign loop.

packets.title: Campaign decisions (delegated by the owner): barter at villages, auto-resolve for lopsided fights, camp overrun as a setback, the 3-D map replaces the retro overworld
packets.acceptance: TAC-K-01 to K-04 in docs/design-decisions/K-campaign.md; campaign roadmap updated; WP-V14 to V16 retired.

packets.title: Ammunition catalogue: real calibres and round types for every tactical weapon, tactical weapons and band gear mapped to catalogue items
packets.acceptance: Every tactical weapon and band weapon resolves to a catalogue weapon, its calibre, its magazines and at least two round types; a test fails on any unmapped id.

packets.title: Golden replays: recorded input streams per level; same seed and inputs give the same debrief
packets.acceptance: tests/replays: one recording per level; a unit test replays each and compares the debrief JSON; documented how to re-record on an intended change.

packets.title: Fuzz harness in the repo: randomised fights over every level, variant and difficulty with invariants
packets.acceptance: npm run fuzz (seeds and duration as flags) checks finite positions and health, bounds, ammunition conservation, single ownership of items, no throws; a short run in npm test, a long one nightly in CI.

packets.title: Performance budgets: sim step and page-load benchmarks with a stored baseline
packets.acceptance: tools/perf: per-level ms per step (mean, p99, worst) and per-page bytes, requests and ready time; docs/perf-baseline.json; a check fails on a regression over 20 %.

packets.title: Every browser suite fails on a console error or an unhandled rejection
packets.acceptance: The shared open() helper records page errors; every suite asserts none at the end; no suppressions without a comment.

packets.title: Campaign save hunt: fuzz normalize and migrate, two tabs, crash between result and settle, quota
packets.acceptance: Property tests over garbage and truncated saves; settle is idempotent across a reload at every step; a second tab never loses the other tab’s writes silently (it warns or merges); quota errors are reported, not swallowed.

packets.title: Inventory hunt: random operation sequences with conservation and ownership invariants
packets.acceptance: Thousands of random move, turn, split, merge, load, unload, reload, fire, loot, eject and use operations; rounds never created or lost; every item in one place; a random-drag browser test on the inventory page.

packets.title: Sim and AI soak: 10-minute fights per level and variant; stuck units, unreachable objectives
packets.acceptance: Detects units stuck for 20 s, units inside cover boxes, objectives that cannot complete, missions with no outcome; each finding fixed or filed.

packets.title: Campaign loop soak: 30 encounters through the pure modules with invariants
packets.acceptance: Deploy, result, settle, clock, healing, parties and settlements over 30 encounters: no negative stash, nobody wounded forever, the log bounded, each result settled once.

packets.title: Input and focus audit across the overlays (encounter, band, kit, search)

packets.title: Firefox and WebKit smoke runs
packets.acceptance: The smoke suite passes in Playwright Firefox and WebKit, or each difference is fixed or documented.

packets.title: Memory leak hunt: restarts, overlays, map and mission trips
packets.acceptance: 50 mission restarts, 100 inventory open and close, 10 map-mission trips: heap and window-listener counts flat; three.js resources disposed.

packets.title: Sim hot path: cached static boxes, a spatial grid for rays and movement, no per-step allocation
packets.acceptance: Golden replays unchanged; worst step under 4 ms on every level; GC under 5 % of sim time; mean step 40 % lower.

packets.title: Compact inventory catalogue: only the kinds the inventory uses

packets.title: Mission renderer: fog of war at a lower rate or incremental, static layers cached

packets.title: Overworld map budget: lazy 3-D figures, texture sizes, draw calls

packets.title: Test suite speed and flake: no fixed sleeps, suites in parallel

packets.title: Static checks: a report of unused exports and unreferenced files; dead code removed
